statements.label: submission must be original work
statements.passage:
We recognize GenAI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, etc.) are ubiquitous and can help you learn, but your submission must be your own original work. In this course, GenAI is a consulting tool, not an author.

You can carefully use GenAI on assignments, but think of GenAI as a peer in the course. Each assignment will have a section to reflect on your usage of GenAI. You must fill this out to receive credit for the assignment, whether or not you used GenAI or not.

We note that in the past, the single best determinator of students’ exam scores was how well they understood the projects. We advise you to not use GenAI as a shortcut on the projects as this may harm your understanding.

Syllabus CSE 420: Design of Operating Systems Fall 2026
(Clarification: AI tools may be used to support learning, but they may not be used to develop as-
signment solutions. Generating pseudocode, algorithms, implementation plans, or similar solution
components is considered AI assistance on the assignment.)
• I pasted my project code into ChatGPT/Gemini/Copilot/R1/Sonnet/Cursor/OthersSimilar and asked
it to find bugs, explain why my solution was not working, or suggest changes to fix it. (Clarification:
AI tools may not be used to review, debug, modify, improve, or otherwise assist with assignment
solutions. Only the course staff may provide solution-specific debugging assistance.)
• I shared my code publicly on GitHub (or other sites) after the course ended. (Clarification: Sharing
your code after the end of the course is still plagiarism.)
To make it crystal clear, here we provide some AI-specific examples showing what is allowed and
what is not:
• Allowed (These are example learning activities. The AI is acting like a textbook, search en-
gine, tutor, or study guide.):
– What does undefined reference to pthread_create mean?
– Explain how semaphores work.
– Generate 20 multiple-choice questions about deadlocks.
– What is the difference between fork() and exec()?
• Not Allowed (In all of these cases, the AI is contributing directly to the assignment solution,
which must be your own intellectual contribution):
– Here is my Project 2 code (or part of it). Why isn’t it working?
– Here’s my implementation. Fix the race condition.
– Give me pseudocode for implementing this scheduler.
– Design the solution approach for this project.
– Generate the code for the file system traversal.
Please note that AI tools may be used as learning resources but may not be used to generate or
assist in the development of assignment solutions. When in doubt, quickly ask the course instructor
via Teams chat before using an AI tool. Students remain responsible for learning and understand-
ing course material. AI-generated information may be inaccurate, incomplete, or inconsistent with
course content, and course lectures, slides, announcements, and instructor guidance take prece-
dence over information obtained from AI tools.

statements.label: AI permitted to some extent
statements.passage:
The use of ChatGPT or other AI tools is permitted to some extent in this class. These tools are being rapidly adopted, so it is important that you have some experience with their use. These tools are best used to help you work smarter, not do your work for you. Remember that an essential part of being in graduate school is to develop skills that you will need to be successful in the workplace. Using aids just to complete an assignment in the quest for high marks will not help you after you leave school.
I encourage you to use these tools to help deepen your understanding and to review material you find challenging. If you use them to blindly do your homework for you, your learning will suffer and it will be obvious. However, using them to clarify concepts, explain errors, or review material can help you learn more effectively.
Students may not submit an entire assignment, homework question, or programming task to a generative AI tool and ask it to produce the answer or solution. AI tools should be used only as learning aids (e.g., asking for explanations of concepts, debugging hints, or clarifications), not as a replacement for your own work.
For all homework assignments, you must include a list of websites or other references that you consult in solving the assignment. This includes AI tools. You must include the website for the tool and either a link to, or screenshot of, the conversation you had with the tool. You must also write out in your homework report the initial prompt that you used.
Note that this policy applies only to CS 471/571 and does not imply that generative AI tools are permitted in other courses

statements.passage:
Use of Machine Learning (“AI”) Tools


Submission of work containing any content generated by Machine Learning tools such as, but not limited to, ChatGPT, Github Copilot, Grammarly AI, etc. is strictly prohibited. This reflects widespread prohibition in the software development industry due to serious and legitimate concerns, such as,

Intellectual Property Rights and Authorship/Attribution

Code Quality and Reliability

Lack of Transparency

Dependency and Lack of Skill Development

Regulatory and Compliance Issues

Ethical and Social Implications

It is relatively easy for experienced programmers to recognize code generated by LLMs like ChatGPT, due to a variety of unusual, inhuman, characteristics, such as poor cohesiveness, repetitiveness, and many other factors that I will not disclose. These traits can be quantified and demonstrated to a sufficient degree for students to be found responsible of Academic Misconduct by an independent investigator. The same holds true for other written works.

As part of the Pomona CS
AI Policy
, this class maintains the Tier 0 level of acceptable AI use. Courses in this tier do not allow the use of any AI. Disallowed uses include, but are not limited to, using generative AI tools to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides, generate code snippets, images, or videos, revise your writing, or check your work. Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed (for example, the spelling and grammar checkers built into Microsoft Word), but not tools that offer suggested revisions of your sentences (for example, Grammarly). If English is not your first language, please ask your instructor about whether tools for translating words or texts between languages are allowed.

The principle behind applying this AI tier is to ensure that your out-of-class help is targeted towards your learning. In general, you are to use your professor and TAs as the primary resource for out-of-class help rather than AI tools.

statements.anchor: AI has no place in the classroom
statements.label: AI replacing thinking unwelcome
statements.passage:
Today's unfortunate reality is that all industries are pushing for their employees to use AI at all costs, despite its devastating social and environmental consequences. While we believe that when used by students to forego critical thinking, AI has no place in the classroom, we understand that students will be expected to use it post-graduation in their careers.

Therefore, this semester, we are allowing (albeit strongly discouraging) students to use AI to assist them on their assignments if they wish. However, we require that students who choose to use any generative AI on their assignments do so responsibly. Specifically, in this course we are
1) requiring that students disclose their AI usage at the time of assignment submission and 2) forbidding students from asking it to generate complete functions and solutions (see
Academic Conduct
below)
.

To clarify, you may use it on small programming tasks that would fall under reasonable usage, such as asking how to use C standard library functions. Additionally, we implore students to verify any information they receive from AI sources, as these can output false information (euphemistically referred to as "hallucinations"). Please contact course staff beforehand if you are unsure whether your intended AI usage is allowed in this class.
